title: Pre-training loss spikes at step 38k and does not recover
situation: A 1B-parameter run (AdamW, bf16, cosine) was smooth for 38k steps, then loss jumped from 2.6 to 5+ and stayed high.

steps.label: Triage
items: Look at grad-norm, per-layer activation max, attention-logit max, loss scale and the exact step; check whether the data at that step was unusual (duplicated, garbage, very long documents).
Compare against the last good checkpoint: restart from it with the same data order. If the spike reproduces, it is data or numerics; if not, it was a rare hardware or race issue.

steps.label: Likely causes
items: Adam second-moment instability: beta2 too high (use 0.95), epsilon too small in bf16.
Attention-logit growth: add QK-norm or logit soft-capping; embedding/LM-head z-loss.
A bad batch: skip it and keep going; learning rate too high late in warmup.

steps.label: Fix
items: Roll back to a checkpoint before the spike, skip the offending data window, lower peak LR 20-30% or add clipping at 1.0, add QK-norm/z-loss for the future.
Add automated spike detection (loss > running mean + k*std) that pauses/rolls back; keep frequent checkpoints.

followups.q: How do you tell a data spike from an optimiser spike?
followups.a: Re-run the same steps with a different data order or skipping that batch: a data-caused spike disappears, an optimiser-state instability returns even with different data, usually preceded by growing gradient and attention-logit norms.

title: CUDA out of memory when fine-tuning a 13B model
situation: Full fine-tuning with AdamW crashes with OOM on a single 80GB GPU.

steps.label: Compute the budget
items: 13B in bf16 weights 26GB + grads 26GB + fp32 master/Adam 156GB = ~208GB before activations - it cannot fit on one 80GB GPU by arithmetic.

steps.label: Options (cheapest first)
items: LoRA/QLoRA: 4-bit frozen base (~7GB) + tiny adapters; fits on one GPU with gradient checkpointing and a short sequence length.
If full fine-tuning is required: FSDP/ZeRO-3 across >=4 GPUs, activation checkpointing, 8-bit optimizers, CPU offload as a last resort.
Reduce activation memory: smaller micro-batch with gradient accumulation, FlashAttention, shorter max sequence length.

steps.label: Validate
items: Do a short smoke run and watch peak memory; confirm quality against a small full-fine-tune baseline on a 1B model before committing.

followups.q: LoRA quality is lower than expected - what next?
followups.a: Raise rank and apply to all linear layers, increase LR (1e-4 to 2e-4), improve data quality, train a bit longer; if the domain shift is large, consider full fine-tuning with sharding or continued pre-training first.

title: After fine-tuning, the model forgot general abilities
situation: A model fine-tuned on 50k domain examples scores well on the domain but dropped 12 points on general benchmarks and refuses simple tasks.

steps.label: Diagnose
items: Compare with the base on general evals before/after; check epochs, LR and whether prompt tokens were in the loss; inspect chat-template and EOS handling.
Look at data diversity: narrow single-format data causes style/format overfitting.

steps.label: Mitigate
items: Lower LR and epochs, use LoRA, mix in 10-30% general instruction/replay data, mask the prompt, add early stopping on a general+domain validation set.
Merge or interpolate weights between the base and the fine-tuned model (WiSE-FT, task arithmetic with scale <1).

followups.q: Why does weight interpolation recover general ability?
followups.a: The fine-tuned weights stay in a linear-mode-connected region of the loss landscape near the pretrained model, so intermediate points trade off new-task gains against retained general capabilities, often with a favourable frontier.

title: Training uses only 30% of GPU capacity
situation: A vision model trains slowly: nvidia-smi shows low utilisation and MFU is ~12%.

steps.label: Profile
items: Use torch.profiler: is the GPU idle waiting for data (dataloader), CPU syncs (.item(), prints), tiny kernels, or communication?
Check dataloader workers, pin_memory, image decoding cost, storage throughput.

steps.label: Fix
items: More workers/prefetch, move augmentation to GPU, cache decoded data, use bf16 + channels-last + torch.compile, bigger batch, remove host-device syncs, fuse ops.
For multi-GPU: overlap communication, check NCCL topology, avoid straggler nodes.

followups.q: MFU is 45% on a single node but 20% on 8 nodes. Why?
followups.a: Inter-node communication (all-reduce/all-gather) is not hidden behind compute: slower interconnect, too small per-GPU batch, FSDP gather overhead. Increase micro-batch/grad accumulation, use hierarchical parallelism (TP in-node), overlap comms, check network health.

title: RLHF run: reward rises but human ratings fall
situation: During PPO the reward-model score climbs steadily, but spot checks show longer, repetitive, flattering answers and a drop in factuality.

steps.label: Confirm
items: Evaluate on held-out human/gold preferences and a different reward model; plot proxy reward vs KL to reference and vs gold score - the classic over-optimisation curve rises then falls.

steps.label: Mitigate
items: Increase KL coefficient or early-stop at peak gold score; length-normalise/penalise length; ensemble reward models; refresh reward data with samples from the current policy; add diversity regularisation.
Consider DPO/online DPO or RLVR with verifiable rewards where possible.

followups.q: How do you explain this to a reviewer?
followups.a: It is Goodhart's law: the reward model is a proxy valid near its training distribution; optimisation pressure exploits its errors. Show the gold-vs-proxy curve, KL budget, and your mitigation ablations.

title: Which adaptation strategy for a new domain?
situation: You must adapt an open 8B LLM to Persian legal text with 20k labelled examples, one 48GB GPU and four weeks.

steps.label: Decide
items: First measure the base model with good prompts and retrieval - sometimes enough. Tokenizer fertility for Persian decides cost; check it.
If domain knowledge/language is weak: continued pre-training (or LoRA on raw text) on in-domain text, then SFT with QLoRA on instructions; keep a general replay mix.
Use RAG for facts that change; fine-tune for style/format/task behaviour.

steps.label: Evaluate
items: Held-out domain test set with human-reviewed gold, general regression benchmarks, and an LLM-judge validated against humans; compare against the prompted base and a retrieval baseline with confidence intervals.

followups.a: A 48GB GPU cannot hold full fine-tuning state for 8B (~130GB); LoRA/QLoRA gets most of the benefit at a fraction of the cost and forgets less, and is easier to iterate and deploy as adapters.
